title: The Quiet Discipline of Journaling
summary: Licensed therapist explores the quiet discipline of journaling — a daily practice to build self-awareness, ease stress, and support mental wellness with Stoic.
body_text: As a therapist, I’m routinely suggesting a journaling practice to my clients. Whether it's reflective journaling, free-association writing, Morning Pages for creativity, or using an app like Stoic, research has repeatedly demonstrated the benefits of journaling to aid our mental wellness. And yet, I'm often surprised how difficult it is for many people to spend just 10 to 20 minutes a day journaling. And honestly, I struggle with it too. Journaling is one of those practices that many of us only fall back to during a crisis. Some unfavorable event happens and suddenly we remember our journal. We open to a blank page, pour out our guts, get brutally honest with ourselves, reflect on recent events, work through irrational thoughts, reconnect with ourselves, and make future plans. For a specific period of time, when things feel urgent, we're devoted to the journaling process. Then the crisis ends. And with it, our journaling practice. But journaling isn't only for times when we're stressed out. It's not just a psychological emergency kit, although, it's very good at that too. Journaling is something to practice everyday. It's best used as an ongoing, quiet practice of self reflection. Regular journaling during times in our lives when things are going well, when life is easy, helps prevent us from unraveling when the stress ramps up. Think of it as a preventative measure. It keeps tension from building into something bigger. I’ve witnessed this over and over again with people who embrace what I call the quiet discipline of daily journaling. The journal entries don’t have to be perfect and they don’t have to be long. They just have to be consistent. My journaling practice is to plan my day with intention in the morning, reflect in the evening, and use journaling prompts throughout the day when something comes up. Not as a crisis-averting technique, but as a grounding one. For me it's akin to stretching. I don’t wait until I've pulled a muscle to start stretching, I stretch daily to keep the soreness and tightness at bay. ‍ How to think about journaling Think of journaling as a mental and emotional stretch. A daily check-in to keep the emotional "soreness and tightness" from creeping in. It doesn’t require a massive commitment. Just five minutes in the morning, maybe another five minutes in the afternoon, and then five minutes in the evening. With Stoic, journaling becomes a kind of structured companion. Instead of scrolling on Instagram, tap on Stoic. Open the Today screen and hit the “Reflect” button. Or go to the Library and scroll until you find a journaling prompt that resonates with you. One of the many things I love about Stoic is how it reflects back and offers different perspectives on my thoughts. It’s creates a subtle, but surprisingly helpful shift in my awareness. I’m no longer writing into a void and the bit of perspective I get from it helps clarify my thinking. And all it takes is for you to decide to show up. You don't need to worry about showing up with perfect words or profound insights, just show up with whatever is going on in your life in the moment. Because starting a quiet discipline of journaling only requires your honesty. Even if you open your journal and start by writing, “I don’t want to be doing this right now,” that’s enough. That sentence is the stretch you may need. And if you stay with it, if you keep writing, even for five minutes at a time, you’ll be surprised where it leads you. And maybe that's why some people don't often think to journal because it doesn't really promise a spectacular finish or some dramatic ending. But what you gain over time is a better relationship with yourself. It's not about self mastery, it's about connecting to self. I encourage you to make a promise to yourself to try journaling for 10-15 minutes a day. Try to stretch your mind out in your journal like you try to stretch your body when you're sore. Let the words flow out of your pen even if those thoughts feel awkward or incomplete. Let the practice of journaling be a place you can focus and find yourself, not only when there's a crisis, but also as a daily reflection. ‍ Try journaling challenge for 7 days Let's try a little experiment, or rather a challenge, if you're up for it. Try journaling for 7 days. Just to see how it feels for you. See how it fits into your life. You can journal with pen and paper, or of course, you can journal inside Stoic. Stoic has many great suggestions for journaling prompts if you would like a little more guidance than just an open page. Again, seven days is all I ask. ‍ Start with this prompt

title: Evaluating the Right eVault: Key Requirements for eNote Compliance
summary: Learn key eNote concepts, including the Authoritative Copy and eVault requirements, to ensure compliance and protect your business from risk.
body_text: With every home loan originated, the borrower signs a promissory note —a negotiable instrument that acknowledges the borrower’s promise to pay the loan pursuant to the terms of the note. For decades, the majority of notes have been executed on paper and wet-ink signed. As the mortgage industry increasingly recognizes the benefits of digitized collateral, particularly for critical documents like the note, the adoption of electronic promissory notes (eNotes) , the digital equivalent of a paper promissory note, continues to increase . While eNotes share many of the same characteristics as its paper counterpart, the legal concepts that govern eNotes differ. As a result, eNotes have unique requirements that must be met. Many of these requirements are supported or enforced by eVaults , the technology used to securely store and manage eNotes. How eNotes Remain Secure and Enforceable Have you ever asked: What legal concepts and requirements govern the use of eNotes? How do these requirements ensure my eNotes remain valid and enforceable? How do they translate into eVault requirements? Asking these questions is an important step if you want confidence that your eVault is compliant and protects your business. Our new white paper, Location Matters: eNote Concepts that Protect Enforceability, Negotiability & Priority , answers these questions by explaining: The significance of the Authoritative Copy of the eNote, and how it is distinguishable from other copies Why certain eNote processes (like converting an eNote to paper) can only be performed against the Authoritative Copy The role of both the eVault and the MERS Ⓡ eRegistry in identifying who maintains the Authoritative Copy, or the “Location” What it means to comply with the MISMO eVault System Standards, and how to determine if an eVault is certified The Right eVault Matters Selecting the right eVault starts with understanding what compliance really means. Historically, it wasn’t easy to tell if an eVault met all requirements. Information was scattered across sources like GSE guidelines, MERS Ⓡ eRegistry procedures, and MISMO specifications. Legal opinions helped provide some clarity, but they only reviewed compliance at a single point in time. But eVaults, as is standard with all technology, undergo system maintenance and enhancements which can impact the way the technology operates. Realizing the industry’s need for alignment and clarity, MISMO established a Development Work Group (DWG) to consolidate eVault standards. This effort resulted in the development of the MISMO eVault System Standards and the MISMO eVault System Standards Certification—a program where eVault providers undergo an annual, third-party review of the eVault’s functionality to verify compliance with these standards, administered by MISMO. This independent certification gives lenders, warehouse lenders, and investors—and any party with interests in eNotes—assurance that their eVault meets the requirements needed to protect the integrity, enforceability, and transferability of their eNotes. At Snapdocs, compliance has always been a key pillar of our innovation. That’s why the Snapdocs eVault is the only eVault certified as compliant with MISMO’s eVault System Standards today —demonstrating our commitment to protecting our customers’ most valuable assets. To confirm the status of an eVault provider’s certification, visit MISMO’s website . Download the full white paper to learn these concepts and how Snapdocs helps lenders protect their eNotes, stay compliant, and realize the full benefits of digital mortgage adoption.

title: Welcome to the Rocket Engineering & Product Blog: Building the Future of Homeownership with AI
summary: Discover how Rocket is leveraging AI to transform the homeownership journey, from innovative technology solutions to reimagining the housing ecosystem with a mission to Help Everyone Home.
body_text: Welcome to the Rocket Engineering & Product Blog: Building the Future of Homeownership with AI Author: Papanii Okai Sep 11, 2025 • 2-minute read Share: Over two decades ago, I was an intern at BEA Systems. Back then, I was both scared and excited. Scared, because there was no plan B, and I had to succeed. I was excited because I was finally solving real problems where no professor had a key with the answers. That experience lit a spark: the realization that technology isn’t just about writing code, it’s about solving human problems. Today, as an executive at Rocket®, I see that same spark in our interns. When they present their summer projects, I’m reminded of my own journey. Only now, they’re starting their careers in an era I could have never imagined back then – the era of artificial intelligence. Why AI Matters Mark Cuban recently said something I couldn’t agree with more: “Understand the fundamentals of computer science but also understand how to apply AI to a business. That’s where the real value lies.” At Rocket, that’s exactly what we’re doing. AI isn’t a buzzword here. It’s the force transforming how we help people achieve the American Dream through one of life’s biggest milestones: homeownership. Most people know us as Rocket Mortgage®. But mortgage is just one part of a much larger ecosystem from technology, financing, titling, underwriting, closing, servicing, real estate, agent networks, broker partnerships, and more. It’s vast, complex, and ripe for transformation. Our mission is simple but bold: Help Everyone Home ... and AI is one of our most powerful tools to deliver on that promise. Where We’re Headed With recent acquisitions like Redfin and the anticipated closing of our acquisition of Mr. Cooper, we’re expanding our reach across the homeownership journey. Together, these platforms generate double digits in petabytes of data, a treasure trove of insight we can responsibly leverage to better serve our clients. But what excites me most are the solutions we’re building right now: A proprietary origination system, now evolving into agentic workflows that make smarter, faster decisions. An agent-powered conversational platform using multiple LLMs, designed to guide clients seamlessly through their journey. Putting AI capabilities directly in the hands of brokers and partners through the use of an in-house generated AI tool. A reimagined Product Development Life Cycle, cutting development time nearly in half leveraging agentic patterns and solutions. And this is only the beginning. We’re collaborating with leaders like AWS, Google, Sierra, Twilio and OpenAI to rethink how AI agents, smart contracts, and automation can reshape the housing ecosystem to be more accessible, inclusive, and simplified for everyone. Collaboration at the Core Our CEO, Varun Krishna, often reminds us: transformation doesn’t happen in isolation. That’s why Rocket is focused on partnership over competition. We’re working with brokers, agents, vendors, and partners so that the ultimate winners are clients and homeowners. At the end of the day, this isn’t just about technology. It’s about people and their pursuit of prosperity. It’s about making the homeownership journey easier, more accessible, and more joyful. What You’ll Find Here This blog is the start of a conversation. In the weeks, months, and years ahead, you’ll see us share: Technical deep dives into systems and our data platform. Product stories about how we’re reimagining client and partner experiences. Lessons learned – what’s worked, what hasn’t, and where we’re heading. Culture highlights from the engineers, designers, and product leaders that are making it happen. We’re opening the doors of Rocket Engineering & Product to show you how we’re building the future; one system, one experiment, one breakthrough at a time. This is just the beginning and we’d love for you to follow along, because the mission to Help Everyone Home is ambitious, and it will take all of us to achieve it. Welcome to the Rocket Engineering & Product Blog. The future of homeownership starts here. Interested in a job at Rocket®? See all of our opportunities today. See Our Jobs Papanii Okai Papanii Okai is the EVP of Product Engineering at Rocket with 20+ years of experience. Previously, he was the CTO at Venmo and held leadership roles at PayPal. A seasoned engineer, he is known for delivering innovative solutions that enhance customer experiences. With a global perspective from living in Africa, Europe and the U.S., he holds degrees in Computer Science and Internet Engineering from University of San Francisco. title: How To Become a Mechanical Contractor
summary: To become a mechanical contractor, you need a combination of education, hands-on training through apprenticeships, relevant certifications, and practical experience in the field
body_text: What is a mechanical contractor? A mechanical contractor is an expert responsible for setting up, maintaining, and repairing mechanical systems in buildings and other structures. These systems include heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC), plumbing, refrigeration, fire protection, and other systems that involve moving parts or fluids. Mechanical contractors play a critical role in construction, ensuring that essential systems are designed, installed, and operated efficiently. Their expertise is crucial in both residential and commercial projects, where they handle everything from the initial design phase to post-construction maintenance. Key Responsibilities of a Mechanical Contractor: Installation of Mechanical Systems : Mechanical contractors are responsible for installing systems like HVAC, plumbing, fire protection, and refrigeration systems. They ensure that all installations comply with building codes and regulations. Maintenance and Repairs : They provide ongoing maintenance for the mechanical systems, ensuring they operate efficiently and effectively throughout their lifespan. Regular inspections and troubleshooting are key parts of the role. System Design and Consultation : In some cases, mechanical contractors are involved in the design phase of a project. They often collaborate with engineers and architects to design and implement systems tailored to the unique requirements of the building. Coordination with Other Trades : Mechanical contractors coordinate with electricians, general contractors, and other professionals to ensure seamless integration of mechanical systems into the broader project. Compliance and Safety : They are responsible for ensuring that all systems are installed according to safety standards, building codes, and local regulations. This includes obtaining the necessary permits and performing safety checks. Mechanical contractors are vital to creating functional, safe, and efficient buildings, making their role indispensable in the construction and maintenance of modern infrastructure. How to become a mechanical contractor Becoming a mechanical contractor requires a mix of education, practical experience, and industry certifications. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to enter this field: 1. Education and Training While formal education is not always required, most mechanical contractors begin by earning a high school diploma or equivalent. However, they often pursue additional training through vocational schools, community colleges, or apprenticeships. This training focuses on key areas such as: HVAC systems Plumbing Refrigeration systems Fire protection systems Pipefitting and ductwork A formal education in mechanical engineering or a related field is also beneficial, especially for those who want to work on larger commercial or industrial projects. 2. Apprenticeship or On-the-Job Experience Most mechanical contractors start their careers as apprentices. As apprentices, they gain practical experience under the guidance of seasoned professionals. Apprenticeships typically last between 3 to 5 years and include a combination of classroom learning and practical, on-the-job experience. Throughout this period, apprentices learn how to install, maintain, and repair mechanical systems while also understanding safety protocols and regulations. 3. Obtain Necessary Licenses and Certifications Depending on the region, mechanical contractors may be required to obtain specific licenses to legally perform certain types of work. Licensing requirements typically involve passing an exam that covers building codes, safety standards, and mechanical system installation. Certifications can enhance credibility and open doors to more lucrative opportunities. 4. Gain Experience and Build a Reputation After completing their apprenticeship or training, individuals often work under a licensed mechanical contractor before starting their own business. Gaining a solid work history, developing skills, and building a good reputation in the industry is critical for long-term success. A mechanical contractor can specialize in specific systems (like HVAC or plumbing) or offer full-service mechanical contracting for both residential and commercial clients. 5. Start Your Own Business Once you have the experience and necessary certifications, you can start your own mechanical contracting business. This includes handling client relationships, supervising projects, recruiting staff, and ensuring adherence to safety regulations and building standards. Starting your own business also requires good management skills, as you’ll need to handle financials, contracts, and marketing, in addition to the technical aspects of mechanical contracting. Duties of mechanical contractors Mechanical contractors are specialized professionals who focus on the installation, maintenance, and repair of mechanical systems in construction projects. Their duties cover a wide range of tasks, each essential to ensuring that the mechanical systems function efficiently and safely within a building or infrastructure. 1. Installation of Mechanical Systems A key responsibility of a mechanical contractor is the installation of various mechanical systems within a construction project. These systems may include: This includes systems such as: HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning) systems designed to regulate indoor air quality and maintain temperature control. Plumbing systems , including water supply and waste management. Fire protection systems , such as sprinklers and alarms. Refrigeration systems , especially for commercial or industrial settings. Other specialized systems like steam and gas piping or exhaust systems. Contractors are responsible for ensuring these systems are correctly installed, following the blueprint and building codes. 2. System Maintenance and Repair Once installed, mechanical contractors are also responsible for the ongoing maintenance and repair of these systems. This includes routine inspections, cleaning, and addressing wear and tear to keep the systems running smoothly. They are responsible for identifying potential issues early and making necessary repairs before they lead to costly breakdowns. 3. Compliance and Safety Ensuring that all mechanical installations comply with local building codes, regulations, and safety standards is another critical responsibility. Mechanical contractors must ensure that systems are safe to operate and meet health and safety standards for building occupants. 4. Project Management and Coordination Mechanical contractors often manage the mechanical aspects of a project, including coordinating with other trades, suppliers, and subcontractors. This involves ensuring that the mechanical systems are completed on time and within budget while aligning with the overall project schedule. 5. Budget and Resource Management Contractors are also responsible for managing the budget and resources for mechanical system installation. This includes estimating costs, sourcing materials, and hiring necessary labor while maintaining cost efficiency. 6. Problem-Solving and Troubleshooting Mechanical contractors must have strong problem-solving skills. They are often called upon to troubleshoot issues with malfunctioning mechanical systems and find solutions quickly to minimize downtime. 7. Client Communication and Reporting A mechanical contractor frequently interacts with clients, providing progress updates, answering queries, and ensuring customer satisfaction. Clear communication is crucial to meet the client’s expectations and ensure the project remains on track. Mechanical Contractor vs. Mechanical Engineer While both mechanical contractors and mechanical engineers work with mechanical systems, their roles in a construction project differ significantly. Here’s a comparison of the two professions: 1. Role and Responsibilities Mechanical Contractor : The main responsibility of a mechanical contractor is to install, maintain, and repair mechanical systems. They handle the physical implementation of the mechanical plans, ensuring systems are properly set up and functional. Contractors often work directly on-site and are involved in the day-to-day management of construction projects. Mechanical Engineer : A mechanical engineer, on the other hand, focuses on the design , planning , and analysis of mechanical systems. They work on developing the systems’ designs and ensuring they function efficiently and safely. Engineers are involved in calculating load capacities, selecting materials, and creating blueprints. They may not directly manage the installation but are involved in guiding the design and specification process. 2. Skills and Education Mechanical Contractor : To become a mechanical contractor, one typically needs practical experience and specialized training, often starting with an apprenticeship. They may need certifications or licenses depending on the region and the systems they install. Contractors also need good project management skills and a strong understanding of safety and compliance standards. Mechanical Engineer : Mechanical engineers usually hold a Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or a related field. Some engineers may pursue further education or certifications to specialize in certain areas, such as HVAC systems or refrigeration. Engineers usually need a solid foundation in physics, mathematics, and design concepts. 3. Project Involvement Mechanical Contractor : Mechanical contractors primarily work on-site, managing the installation and maintenance of mechanical systems. They collaborate closely with the construction team and oversee daily activities. Mechanical Engineer : Engineers are generally involved during the design and planning phases of the project. They create the technical specifications, select materials, and ensure the design meets both functional and regulatory standards. Engineers often guide the contractors during installation and conduct evaluations after completion. 4. Work Environment Mechanical Contractor : Mechanical contractors spend most of their time on-site, overseeing the installation and repair of mechanical systems. They work directly with the construction team and handle day-to-day operations. Mechanical Engineer : Engineers typically work in offices or design studios, where they focus on drafting plans and calculations. They may visit the construction site occasionally to supervise installations or assess completed work. 5. Decision-Making Authority Mechanical Contractor : Contractors often have decision-making authority on-site regarding how systems are installed, managing resources, timelines, and budget. Mechanical Engineer : Engineers make critical decisions related to the design , functionality , and efficiency of mechanical systems. They ensure that all designs meet the required standards but usually have less direct involvement in the hands-on aspects of the project. Next Read: How to Become a Concrete Contractor

title: Hugh Hollar Inducted into the Home Builders Association of Georgia Hall of Fame
summary: Hugh Hollar of Colony Bank is inducted into the Home Builders Association of Georgia Hall of Fame, recognizing his industry impact.
body_text: Colony Bank is proud to announce that Hugh Hollar, Senior Vice President and Director of Homebuilder Finance, has been inducted into the Home Builders Association of Georgia (HBAG) Hall of Fame, the Association’s highest honor. The Hall of Fame Award recognizes individuals whose careers embody excellence, leadership, and an unwavering commitment to the homebuilding industry. Induction is a rare distinction, reserved for those who have made a lifetime of impact. With more than 36 years of service to the homebuilding industry, Hollar has played a key role in expanding builder financing opportunities and strengthening access to housing across Georgia and the Southeast. At Colony Bank, he has developed programs that provide one-stop builder financing, from construction loans through to mortgages, and built a team with over 125 years of combined experience. Beyond his work at Colony Bank, Hollar has served on the board of the Home Builders Association Greater Aiken-Augusta Region for more than three decades, where he has been honored as Associate Member of the Year 3 times and received the Shining Star Award at both the local and state level. He has also represented Georgia on the national stage through his involvement with the National Association of Home Builders. Hollar’s impact extends well beyond the industry. He has served on the Development Authority of Columbia County, the board of the Burn Foundation of America, worked with the Coalition of Quality Government and the Merchants Association of Columbia County, and volunteered with The Bridge Ministry of the CSRA. He also served in various leadership positions at First Baptist Church of Augusta, currently serving as a Trustee and a Deacon. Commenting on the announcement, Ed Canup, Chief Banking Officer, EVP, said, “Hugh’s induction into the Hall of Fame is a testament to the impact he has made throughout his career. We are fortunate to have his leadership at Colony Bank and grateful for the positive impact he continues to make on our customers, our team, and our communities. We are proud to celebrate this recognition alongside him.” News Share this:

title: Why Learning a Language Is Key to Deeper Cultural Understanding
summary: Language and culture. Go deep into both and learn with Univerbal.
body_text: Learning a language offers more than proficiency in grammar and vocabulary. It unlocks doors to new ways of thinking, behaving, and connecting - enriching your understanding of other cultures and your own place in the world. In this guide, discover how language and culture are connected, real-life examples, practical intercultural learning strategies, and how Univerbal empowers you to become a true global citizen. How language and culture connect: real-life examples Benefits of cultural understanding through language learning Practical tips for cultural learning How Univerbal facilitates cultural learning Frequently Asked Questions Conclusion How language and culture connect: real-life examples Language and culture develop side-by-side, each influencing and reflecting the other in unique ways. When you learn a new language, you also learn: How people express values and emotions What concepts are important in their society Rituals, etiquette, and “unspoken rules” Examples 🇯🇵 Japanese – The term “Mono no Aware” (物の哀れ): Embodying appreciation for the fleeting nature of life, present in poetry, hanami (cherry blossom viewing), and daily expressions about transience and reflection. The cherry blossoms in Japan encapsulate the concept of “Mono no Aware” 🇩🇰 Danish – “Hygge” : This untranslatable word means much more than “coziness” - it celebrates bonding, warmth, and well-being in Danish homes. 🇪🇸 Spanish – Phrases like “mi casa es tu casa” (“my house is your house”) show family importance and hospitality. Affectionate terms such as “corazón” (heart) and “cariño” (dear) reflect warmth in everyday life. 🇫🇷 French – A rich lexicon for bread and cheese ( baguette , boule , camembert ) reveals the deep significance of food, craftsmanship, and tradition. 😌 A ‘baguette’, ‘boule', ‘bâtard’ and ‘pain complet’ - the French really love their bread! Benefits of cultural understanding through language learning Learning a language always includes learning culture. The advantages: Empathy : See the world through another’s eyes, recognize and respect differences. Broader Perspective : Understand customs and history that shape outlooks on life and success. Travel, Work, Life : Navigate international environments with greater ease and confidence. Better Communication : Catch idioms, jokes, and subtle cues, avoiding misunderstandings. Cross-cultural knowledge gives you tools for social intelligence and real global connection. Learn more about the unique specifics of intercultural communication in this video . Practical tips for cultural learning Engage with native speakers Practice with native speakers - online or in-person - gives you real insights you’ll never get from a textbook. Not able to travel? Univerbal provides a safe, supportive environment for virtual practice until you’re ready for real-life conversations. Immerse yourself in media Media is a window into what matters in a culture. Movies & TV : Experience the humor, drama, and worldview (e.g., Bollywood’s color, K-Dramas’ plots, French cinema’s nuance). Music & Literature : Learn slang, references, and social themes first-hand. Take part in cultural events Join festivals and traditions, onsite or virtually. Examples: The Indian festival of Holi for color and renewal, Venice Carnival for artistry, Spanish cooking classes, and Mid-Autumn mooncake traditions in East Asia. Events and celebrations are tactile, sensory experiences—take part and learn directly! Festivals and events can give you a unique glimpse into the local culture How Univerbal facilitates cultural learning Univerbal doesn’t just teach words or grammar. It: Embeds cultural nuance and context in lessons and dialogues. Simulates real-life scenarios like etiquette, traditional celebrations, and local customs. Offers AI-powered feedback during practice Even if you don’t have native speakers at home, Univerbal bridges that gap - right from your phone. Learn about culture with your AI conversation partner if you don’t have a native speaker to practice with. Get instant feedback on every message and correct it straight away. Frequently Asked Questions Q: Why is learning a language important for cultural understanding? A: Language is a direct reflection of culture - learning it allows you to understand what matters, how people think, and how society functions. Q: How can I learn about culture if I can’t travel? A: Practice with native speakers online, use language exchange, participate in global events virtually, and immerse yourself in international films, media, and books. Q: Does Univerbal help with cultural learning too? A: Yes! It integrates context and real-life scenarios into dialogues, helping you understand both words and the meaning behind them. Q: Will learning a language make me more empathetic? A: Yes - multiple studies show that learning languages builds empathy, adaptability, and communication skills. Conclusion Every language you learn is a new lens on humanity. With Univerbal, you not only speak new words but open yourself to new experiences, ideas, and friendships. title: Fresenius Medical Care Celebrates Nephrology Nurses Week with The CARE Award
body_text: Fresenius Medical Care (FME), the world's leading provider of products and services for individuals with renal diseases, celebrates nurses for the vital role they play in improving the quality of life of patients every day. During Nephrology Nurses Week (September 14-20, 2025), FME reaffirms the commitment to professional growth and patient-centered care to ensure long-term resilience and quality patient care, which play a key role in the “ FME Reignite ” corporate strategy. “Our patients are at the heart of everything we do, and our nurses are beside them every step of the way, fostering strong relationships that impact every aspect of the patient's experience,” said Michelle Carver , Chief Nursing Officer and Senior Vice President, Nursing & Clinical Services. “As we celebrate nephrology nurses, we also recognize the vital need to care for the caregiver and continue supporting the well-being of our nurses.” Fresenius Medical Care offers comprehensive support, education, learning and development of nurses, including offering best practices, innovation, and practical advice for caregivers who support people with chronic kidney disease. To honor nurses, the company continues to prioritize their growth, professional development, and career advancement. As part of Nephrology Nurses Week, FME is also honoring care teams with The CARE (Caring About Renal Excellence) Award. The CARE Award is awarded annually to exceptional care team members who deliver unwavering commitment to providing exceptional care. Nephrology nurses receive The CARE Award during Nephrology Nurses Week, observed every year in mid-September. At The CARE Award annual recognition event, FME celebrates committed nephrology care team members who embody clinical excellence and have exemplified mastery in one of the following clinical pillars: quality and safety, growth, clinical leadership, clinical excellence, and patient experience. The CARE Award brings together hundreds of care team members from across the U.S., each nominated by their peers, leaders, and patients.

title: Rebalance Don’t Retreat: Alternative Strategies to Help You Stay Invested
summary: Calamos alternative offerings are designed to navigate volatility, with the goal of providing a steadier ride through choppy equity markets. In this post, we highlight two of our innovative solutions—which can work independently or in tandem to help address investor needs.
body_text: Rebalance Don’t Retreat: Alternative Strategies to Help You Stay Invested September 15, 2025 Summary points: September has a reputation for being a scary month for the markets—but with the right asset allocation in place, it doesn’t have to be a scary time for investors. Calamos alternative offerings are designed to navigate volatility, with the goal of providing a steadier ride through choppy equity markets. In this post, we highlight two of our innovative solutions—which can work independently or in tandem to help address investor needs. Calamos Hedged Equity Fund (CIHEX) leverages a dynamic options overlay seeking to capture equity market upside, while actively dampening downside, allowing investors to stay invested without absorbing the full brunt of market drawdowns. Calamos Autocallable Income ETF (CAIE) utilizes laddered autocallable notes with high coupon income (equity linked) to pursue high, stable monthly income; autocallable structure provides barriers that help mitigate principal loss. While each fund offers standalone benefits, a combination of CIHEX and CAIE can go a step further to help address investors’ key goals and concerns—income with reduced sensitivity to interest rates, exposure to market upside with less vulnerability to drawdowns, and the potential to enhance overall portfolio resilience. It’s not surprising that investors feel uneasy in September—historically, it’s been the worst month to be invested in equities. Since 1950, the S&P 500 Index has averaged a 0.72% decline in September, and over the last decade, September has averaged an even worse -2% decline. Regardless of whether history repeats in 2025, there’s no doubt that investors have plenty to contend with this September: persistent inflation could spook the Fed from lowering rates later this month; low bond yields create a murky backdrop for income-oriented investors; and anxiety about slowing growth and stretched valuations have buffeted tech stocks. Not surprisingly, we’ve seen many of the classic hallmarks of jittery markets: gold surged past $3,500, and the 30-year Treasury yield rose to 4.98%, reflecting a shift toward defensive assets as investors appear to be repositioning after a strong summer rally. The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) jumped, crossing the 18 threshold, signaling elevated investor anxiety and potential for further downside. Rebalance Don’t Retreat: Calamos Alternative Solutions Built to Address Volatility In markets like these, we believe the best course is to find the right strategies that make it easy to stay invested. Since its founding in the 1970s, Calamos has sought to provide investors with the opportunity to capitalize on volatility, introducing a range of innovative alternative approaches in ETF and mutual fund structures. Below, we highlight two—Calamos Hedged Equity Fund (CIHEX) and Calamos Autocallable Income ETF (CAIE). Both CIHEX and CAIE have distinguished themselves amid recent market turbulence by combining income generation with sophisticated risk management. This dual advantage has led both funds to outperform many traditional equity and income peers to date. Calamos Hedged Equity Fund Calamos Autocallable Income ETF Investor focus If the focus is on downside risk mitigation with potential upside capture, then CIHEX. If the focus is on pursuing potentially higher income than traditional dividend stocks and equity market exposure, then CAIE What the Fund seeks Meaningful participation in equity market upside seeking to contain drawdowns. Total return while potentially enhancing current income through high, stable monthly income Key Points During the first half of 2025, CIHEX captured over 70% of the S&P 500’s 2% gain while containing drawdowns. 4-star Morningstar Overall Rating.* Three-year beta of 0.52 vs S&P 500 based on Morningstar data from 9/1/2022-8/31/2025 Standard deviation approximately half (53%) of the S&P 500 Index over the 3 years ending June 30, 2025. Distribution rate of 13.77% as of 8/31/2025. Performance since inception reflected healthy coupon payment rates, with 100% of live autocallables paying coupons as of late August. Since inception, CAIE has delivered strong NAV and price returns (over 6% since inception as of 7/31/25), while accepting equity-like standard deviation (targets 20–22%). How the Fund works Leverages a dynamic options overlay to capture equity market upside, while actively dampening downside, allowing investors to stay invested without absorbing the full brunt of market drawdowns. Active options management drives results; flexible options-driven hedge is rebalanced on an ongoing basis. The fund’s current “65/35” options overlay (targeting 65% market upside, 35% downside) has allowed tactical trades—especially put options—around the core position. Coupons typically higher than bonds, tied to equity market performance. Autocallable structure introduces “barriers”—protection levels such that principal losses only occur if the reference index drops more than 40% from each note’s inception and remains there at maturity. By holding over 50 notes with staggered maturities, the fund reduces timing and reinvestment risk, seeking a smoother income profile even during episodic equity volatility. Contingent income and principal protection features are sensitive to deep, protracted equity market declines. Past performance is no guarantee of future results. Overall Morningstar Rating™ among 131 Equity Hedged funds. The Fund’s risk-adjusted returns based on load-waived Class I shares had 4 stars for 3 years, 3 stars for 5 years and 4 stars for 10 years out of 131, 98 and 57 Equity Hedged Funds, respectively, for the period ended 8/31/2025. Standard deviation for three years ending June 30, 2025 was 8.3% for CIHEX and 15.8% for the S&P 500 Index. A Compelling Complementary Combination for Uncertain Times Together, the funds offers the potential for growth and income with an opportunity for risk mitigation against market fluctuations in uncertain market conditions. In conclusion Periods of heightened uncertainty present critical decision points for investors. Rather than retreating, we believe these conditions call for thoughtful repositioning. Solutions like CIHEX and CAIE are designed to help investors remain engaged with markets, actively manage downside risk, and pursue meaningful income—all while maintaining long-term objectives. This balanced approach empowers investors to navigate volatility proactively and with confidence, making CIHEX and CAIE compelling solutions for portfolio resiliency and growth. title: Vooma Schedule - Automating every appointment
summary: Q3 Product Release - Discover how Vooma Schedule now handles emails, portals, and auto-booking so your team spends less time chasing confirmations.
body_text: Scheduling loads has always been a slow process – think long email chains, logging into different portals, and chasing confirmations. It takes time, causes delays, and pulls teams away from more important work. That’s why we’re rolling out major updates to Vooma Schedule . Now, appointments can be booked automatically over email, confirmed directly in leading portals, or triggered the moment your TMS marks a shipment ready . Vooma also learns from your past schedules to suggest the best times and will soon let you confirm multiple appointments in a single step with batch scheduling . Together, these changes make scheduling faster, simpler, and far less manual . Email scheduling Scheduling loads by email shouldn’t take hours of back-and-forth. With Vooma Schedule, your team can confirm appointments in minutes. Automatic booking : Our AI negotiates appointment times over email within your time windows. No more chasing : If a carrier doesn’t reply, Vooma follows up automatically until it’s confirmed. Better rates, fewer mistakes : Lock in preferred times faster and avoid costly delays. Always updated : Every change shows up instantly in your TMS and Slack/Teams. Portal scheduling Some carriers and shippers require scheduling through web portals or APIs. Vooma handles these too. Hands-free scheduling : Our AI agents log into portals, click through pages, and book times on your behalf. Reliable and fast : No need to juggle logins or remember multiple workflows. Vooma books it for you. Deep integrations : We connect directly with the systems you use most, including: Blue Yonder DSDLink E2open LMConnect Manhattan NCR Opendock Rydershare Yardview And if you don’t see your portals listed, no worries. Our team makes it easy to set up additional integrations so you can plug in the tools that matter most to your operations. Just reach out, and we’ll get you connected. With email and portal scheduling covered, your team can focus on moving freight – not managing calendars. Auto-scheduling Vooma brings true end-to-end automation to scheduling . When shipment data is passed from your TMS, Vooma detects that the load is ready to schedule and begins the process automatically. The agent communicates with locations over email or navigates portals directly, completing bookings without human intervention. This means shipments get scheduled the moment they’re ready , your team stays focused on higher-value work, and you lock in the best appointment times without the usual back-and-forth. Smart timing Over time, Vooma learns which appointment times work best for each location based on your past scheduling history. That means when Vooma is booking appointments automatically, it can suggest or secure the slots that are most likely to be accepted, saving your team from unnecessary changes and making scheduling even smoother. Coming soon We’re adding even more ways to take the work out of scheduling. Soon, you’ll see Batch Scheduling , which lets you confirm several appointments in a single email. We’re also working on smarter time suggestions and deeper TMS integrations so scheduling feels faster and easier every step of the way. Get started with Schedule If you’re already a Vooma Schedule customer, you can start saving time and steps with the new features. Sign up for a Demo to get started with Schedule now.

title: 6 Packaging Insights That Competitive Brands Adopt to Attract Gen Z
summary: Born between the late 90s and early 2010s, the generation referred to as ‘Gen Z’ has grown up fully in the digital age. To help brands looking to attract this consumer base, Sonoco Metal Packaging EMEA partnered with trends agency, Groupe Caramel, to study how packaging influences Gen Z purchasing behavior.
body_text: Gen Z expects more from products—sustainability, visual appeal and a reflection of their values. Born between the late 90s and early 2010s, the generation referred to as ‘Gen Z’ has grown up fully in the digital age. They’re tech-savvy, socially conscious and highly connected to global, ‘big picture’ issues. To help brands looking to attract this consumer base, Sonoco Metal Packaging EMEA partnered with trends agency, Groupe Caramel, to study how packaging influences Gen Z purchasing behavior. Groupe Caramel CEO, Virginie Lorenzato, shares, “Gen Z no longer just buys a product. They choose an experience, a story, a stance. As a result, packaging becomes a cultural medium—a space for expression, emotion and connection.” Packaging Insight #1: Affordable Indulgence Gen Z sees premium packaging as a symbol of quality, pleasure and self-care. By adopting pleasing packaging, tinned fish and other pantry staples continue to grow in popularity. According to Ad Age, 81% of Gen Z tried a product because of standout packaging, and 63% have made repeat purchases for the same reason. By designing metal-packaged products to appeal, brands can tap into Gen Z’s desire for indulgence at accessible price points. Packaging Insight #2: Personal Aesthetics Gen Z views packaging as an extension of their personal style. With 60% of younger consumers claiming finishes influence their purchasing decisions, incorporating design-led formats like polished or matte finishes , vintage-styling, retro typography or collectible packaging can outperform plainer alternatives and appeal to Gen Z’s personal taste. Packaging Insight #3: Social Centerpiece Gen Z combines intentionality and home comfort. According to a 2025 European study, 63% of Gen Z prefer to gather at home over public spaces. By adopting visually appealing, creative designs in both single-serve and shareable formats, metal packaging supports everyday restocking, low-pressure social gatherings or solo-dining rituals—balancing practicality, aesthetic value and recycling. Packaging Insight #4: Flexibility Gen Z values portable and planet-friendly choices that flex with their lifestyle. In 2024, on-the-go containers accounted for 27.5% of the total food storage market. With easy-open features like Sonoco’s Orbit™ metal lid , brands can ensure a successful customer experience while incorporating strong visuals that reinforce sustainability messaging. Additionally, as plant-forward diets like flexitarianism grow in popularity among Gen Z, canned tomatoes, beans and other vegetables offer long shelf life and convenience. Packaging Insight #5: Premium and Purpose Gen Z resonates with clear and credible sustainability. According to a McKinsey study, 60% of Gen Z prefer recyclable packaging and often perceive metal as the most environmentally responsible choice. Across generations, 82% of European consumers are more likely to buy a product if it comes in metal packaging and 70% are willing to pay a 15–20% premium for recyclable metal tins. To reinforce their sustainability commitments, brands can incorporate packaging designs to reinforce their environmental commitments or increasingly popular refillable packaging formats. Packaging Insight #6: Identity and Values Gen Z increasingly looks for products that reflect identity, cultural and shared values. 65% prefer packaging that conveys authenticity and tradition, while 45% are drawn to collectible formats that connect with fandoms, rituals or niche communities. Limited edition metal packaging formats become a method of storytelling—transforming a product into a keepsake, conversation starter or symbol of belonging. As Gen Z embraces the ironic, playful, exaggerated and often ridiculous, surreal graphics, absurd humor and unexpected formats act as an expression of everything from authenticity to joyful escapism. Apply Findings into Desirable, Sustainable Packaging Concepts with Sonoco Stay current with Gen Z’s evolving expectations alongside the leading provider of metal packaging solutions worldwide! With a deep portfolio and global footprint that now includes EMEA, Sonoco’s in-house design studio and R&D center combine technical performance and design thinking to create packaging that connects emotionally and culturally while delivering sustainability, delighting current consumers and recruiting new ones. Learn more about Sonoco’s world-class metal solutions and services !
